payload.caveat: Narrative order follows the publication; exact experiment dates were not reported.
payload.objective: Represent the weak-fragment, linking, linker-length, and cellular-activity branches reported in the study.

payload.message: Record the crystallographic weak Site 1 lead.

payload.interpretation: Weak, but soluble and structurally confirmed in Site 1.

payload.rationale: The weak compound was retained because its core was tractable, soluble, and crystallographically validated.

payload.message: Record the complementary weak Site 2 fragment.

payload.rationale: Retained as a complementary Site 2 anchor despite weak isolated affinity.

payload.statement: Link the meta position of compound 4 to the sulfonamido nitrogen of fragment 5.

payload.message: Link the two weak binders with the initial 10.6 Å design.

payload.result: >10,000-fold improvement over either fragment; BCL-2 Ki 2.0 nM and BCL-xL Ki <1 nM.

payload.rationale: The linking hypothesis produced the intended affinity jump.
Selected as the lead for subsequent optimization because it combined subnanomolar binding with measurable cellular activity.
Excellent biochemical affinity did not translate to cellular activity.
The rigid ethynyl linker retained binding but not useful cellular activity.
The shorter linker weakened affinity and retained poor cellular activity.
Added linker flexibility cost at least an order of magnitude in affinity.
Changing attachment geometry reduced BCL-2 affinity relative to compound 7.

payload.message: Remove the non-interacting dihydroxybutyl side chain.

payload.result: BCL-2 and BCL-xL Ki <1 nM; H146/H1417 cell growth IC50 0.43/0.65 µM.

payload.rationale: Truncating a non-interacting side chain preserved binding and improved cellular activity.

payload.message: Add the ethyl pocket-fill modification and advance the optimized inhibitor.

payload.result: BCL-2 and BCL-xL Ki <1 nM; H146/H1417 cell growth IC50 60–90 nM.

payload.rationale: Reported as the best compound after biochemical affinity translated to cellular activity.
